# Task: Ask-the-book chat for uploaded books, plus friend-code field after a file is picked

Worktree: this repo, branch feat/upload-pictures (already has pictures/panels/vault for uploaded `u-` books and friend codes). Build on it.

## Part A: chat for uploads (main goal)
Today chat is shelf-only: `app/reader.tsx` sets `chatOn = !isUploadId(bookId)`, and `server/chat/handler.ts` rejects ids that fail `isKnownBookId` and loads via `loadBookData` (shelf only). Change it so uploaded books get chat with exactly the same behaviour as shelf books:
1. `server/chat/handler.ts`: accept `isKnownBookId(id) || isUploadId(id)` (from `@/core/uploads`). Load the book via `loadBook` from `@/server/books` (shelf + finished uploads), injectable through a new optional `deps.loadBook?: (bookId: string) => Promise<BookPayload>` like `server/images/handler.ts` does. A missing/expired/unfinished upload (loadBook throws notFound) must answer 400 `bad_request` with the generic message, never a throw/404/500, and must refund the quota it took (or check the book before taking quota; pick the simpler correct option — loading before quota is fine since it costs no Meta money, but don't let an unknown id consume quota).
2. Keep everything else identical for uploads: same `buildChatSystemPrompt` (same kind "the book has not said so yet" fallback), same spoiler gate `bookTextUpTo(book.paragraphs, book.chapters, body.upToN, body.spoilers)` with the clamp, same per-person dual quota (`CHAT_DAILY_LIMIT` / `CHAT_BYOK_DAILY_LIMIT`), same spend reserve on our key, same BYOK header path (reader key skips our spend reserve, still takes quota, never logged/echoed). Book text is untrusted: it must stay inside the existing delimited data block of the system prompt; do not add book text anywhere else (e.g. not in logs, not in error messages). Logs keep book id only.
3. `app/reader.tsx`: mount `ReaderChat` for uploads too (drop the gate; update the comment).
4. `app/chat/reader-chat.tsx`: when the reader finished the upload with their own key, `getReaderKey(bookId)` from `app/leer/reader-key.ts` returns it (module memory only). Use it as the initial BYOK key for chat on that book, so their questions go on their key. Keep the existing memory-only rule. Closing the panel currently clears `byokKey`; for an upload key from reader-key memory, after close fall back to that reader key again (not null) — simplest: compute `const effectiveKey = byokKey ?? getReaderKey(bookId)` and pass that to useChat and ChatPanel. Never persist or log it.
5. Fix comments that say chat is shelf-only (`server/books.ts` loadBookData comment, `app/reader.tsx`).

Tests (mock Meta, Blob, Redis, Turnstile; no network):
- server chat: an upload id served through injected `loadBook` gets a streamed answer, the system prompt contains only text up to upToN (a marker paragraph after upToN must NOT appear in the upstream messages when spoilers are off), quota taken; a missing upload answers 400 bad_request and takes no quota / refunds it; an upload with BYOK header uses the reader key for the streamer and reserves no spend. Put these in a NEW file `server/chat/handler-uploads.test.ts` (handler.test.ts is near the size limit), reusing `server/chat/test-fixtures.ts` helpers.
- `app/reader-upload.test.tsx`: flip the "hides chat for an upload id" test to "mounts chat for an upload id" and update the file's header comment.
- reader-chat: a test that with a reader key set via `setReaderKey`, the chat request carries the BYOK header (or that useChat receives the key) — keep it small, in an existing chat test file if it fits the size limit, otherwise a new small file.

## Part B: friend-code field after a file is picked (only if simple)
`app/home/upload.tsx` shows "Have a friend code?" / the "Friend code" input only on the idle screen. Extract that block into a small component (same file or `app/home/friend-code.tsx`) and also render it on the parsed screen (after a file is picked, both for the free route and the BYOK route, under the book card, above the actions), and in `FailedView` for `daily_books_reached` (there, add a quiet "Try with friend code" action that retries `onRetry` without a key when a code is entered). The code stays in state only; same input attributes (maxLength 64, autoComplete off, spellCheck false). The route already re-evaluates: `uploadRoute(words, friendCode.trim() ? 0 : freeCount)` so typing a code on the BYOK screen switches to the free route — that's desired. Add a test in `app/home/upload.test.tsx` (or a new small test file if the size limit bites) that the friend field is reachable after a file is picked. Keep copy warm; never the word "Generated".

## Out of scope
Do not build narration/read-aloud or music for uploads. Don't touch pictures code.
## Rules (all mandatory)
- Repo: lectoria (Next.js 16, React 19, vitest). Read AGENTS.md first and follow it.
- Do NOT commit, push, deploy or create branches. Just edit files in this worktree; I review and commit.
- Never read, print or copy .env* files or any secret. Tests must mock Meta, Blob, Redis, Turnstile; no real network calls.
- Never load production music. Do not start dev/prod servers (I do browser checks myself). Don't kill any process you didn't start.
- Keep every file under the repo's size limit (run `npm run check:size`). Split modules if needed.
- UI rules: light mode default, Meta blue #0866FF, never purple. English, warm copy, never the word "Generated". Boxless buttons that still read as clickable. Animate only on hover/click/state change; respect prefers-reduced-motion (no transition under reduce). Keep the string "Bring your own key!" exactly as is.
- Small, focused diff. No unrelated refactors. Add/adjust unit tests for behavior you change.
- Before finishing run: `npm run typecheck`, `npx vitest run`, `npm run check:size`, `npm run check:secrets`. All must pass.
- Final answer: a short summary of what you changed (files) and anything you skipped and why.
- Also run `npx eslint <files you touched>`: introduce no new lint errors in files you touch.
- Be economical: explore only what you need, don't re-read big files repeatedly, don't print huge outputs.

50|| Situation | Skill |
51||-----------|-------|
52|| Designing a task | `architect` |
53|| Before writing logic | `principle-foundational-thinking`, `principle-type-system-discipline` |
54|| Writing TypeScript | `typescript-best-practices` |

56|| Debugging | `principle-fix-root-causes` |
57|| Finishing a task | `principle-prove-it-works` |

70|

77|- The emotion taxonomy has 8 ASCII ids: calma, alegria, tristeza, suspenso, misterio, aventura, combate, asombro. 78|- Jev runs at `POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone` with the model pinned to `jev-1.14.0`.
79|- Public-domain books only.
80|- Images follow the book text and the W. W. Denslow 1900 illustrations: silver shoes, nothing from the 1939 MGM film.
81|- Never copy code from github.com/martinmw13/lectoria.
82|- Test with the cheapest models (Contributor). Use Standard for the final pass and the public chat.

84|## Product rules
85|
86|Owner decisions. Short and binding.
87|
88|- Desktop first. No mobile or iOS work now.
89|- The reader shows one scene at a time. Sub-pages split long scenes by length only. Music cues run on scene entry.
90|- A chapter holds several scenes. Each scene has its own emotion.
91|- Paragraph ids carry a global ordinal `n`. Compare `n`, never id strings.
92|- `book.json` is frozen with a `textVersion` hash. Every cache key includes it.
93|- Scenes cover each chapter's paragraphs with no gaps and no overlaps. No scene crosses a chapter boundary. Scenes split at strong sequential emotion shifts; blends stay in the vector.
94|- Emotions are distributions. Each scene stores the full Jev probability vector over the 8 ids, plus `intensity` (0 to 1) and `tempo` (energy, 0 to 1). The Muse override on low confidence edits the vector and records that it did. It never swaps in a single label.
95|- Music is about 15 tracks, pre-generated offline with MusicGen on Modal as one coherent soundtrack: same orchestra and instrumentation, same leitmotif style. Each track is a weighted blend of emotions and carries an emotion vector plus intensity and tempo. The proposed way to pick the blends: cluster the Oz scene vectors and use the centroids as track prompts.
96|- The player picks the track nearest to the scene vector, by cosine similarity over the vector plus intensity and tempo. Hysteresis stops it from flipping on small changes. Skip or change track overrides until the next scene.
97|- The owner listens to short clips before any full generation. Agents do not run Modal until the owner says so.
98|- MusicGen weights are CC-BY-NC. The hackathon demo is non-commercial. The generated tracks must say so in their README.
99|- Chat is low priority and simple. The context is the book text up to the reader's current position. The book prefix goes first and the question goes last, so readers share the prompt cache. Oz is about 55k tokens.
100|- The chat system prompt answers only from the provided text. It refuses knowledge beyond it, even if the model knows the book.
101|- A spoiler mode toggle is for readers who finished the book. It sends the whole text so they can ask about later events. No live Glimmer spoiler guard. No per-chapter summaries for chat. Citing passages is optional.
102|- Glimmer (open weights) keeps a pipeline role. Current decision: it writes the per-scene "why this music" explanation shown in the Developer View.
103|- Spikes come before feature code. Throwaway scripts in `scripts/spikes/` measure Muse Image (response format, latency, Denslow-style prompt), Meta `json_schema` structured output, and the Jev vector on a few Oz scenes. Results go to `docs/spikes.md`.
104|- Spend is counted in integer micro-dollars. Reserve with Redis `INCRBY` before each model call and refund with `DECRBY` after. Reserve per call, including retries.
105|- The server clamps every model tool argument. Tool arguments are untrusted input.
106|- The CSP allows `challenges.cloudflare.com` (script and frame) and `*.public.blob.vercel-storage.com` (images).
107|- The "Picture this" cache key is the book plus the selection's paragraph range plus `textVersion` plus `promptVersion`. A selection that overlaps a cached range in the same scene with paragraph Jaccard at least 1/3 reuses that image; a much larger, smaller, or disjoint one gets its own. The prompt is built from the selected paragraphs plus scene context.
108|- Chapter panels (one comic page per chapter) are drawn only for chapters the reader has reached: requests carry `reachedCh` and the server refuses `ch > reachedCh`. It is the client's claim, since there is no server-side reading position.
109|- The "Picture scene" cache key is the book plus the scene id plus `textVersion` plus `promptVersion`.
110|- Images live in Vercel Blob at deterministic public paths (`addRandomSuffix: false`, `allowOverwrite: false`). An index in Upstash Redis maps key to Blob URL so hits are one Redis GET; on an index miss check the Blob path with `head()` before generating and backfill the index. Routes return Blob URLs, never image bytes.
111|- Modal endpoints require proxy auth. Tokens live only in env.
112|
113|## Security rules
114|
115|Summary. The full rules live in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).
116|
117|- Secrets live only in env vars: `.env.local` locally (gitignored), Vercel env vars in prod.
118|- `.env.example` holds names only, never values.
119|- Never use a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variable for a secret. Only public ids such as the Turnstile site key may use it.
120|- `core/` stays pure: no keys, no env reads, no network clients, no `server-only`. Key-holding clients live in `server/` (Next.js only, each file starts with `import 'server-only'`) and in `pipeline/` (Node scripts that read env). Callers inject them into `core` functions as arguments. Tests run `core` with fake clients.
121|- The pre-commit secret scan must pass. Never bypass it with `--no-verify`.
122|- Errors to the client are generic. Details go to server logs only, never with keys.
123|- Never log request headers.
124|
125|## Writing rules
126|
127|Run docs, UI copy, and commit messages through the `unslop` skill: no filler, no hype, no emoji in headings, none of seamless, elevate, delve, robust, leverage. Headings use sentence case. Commit messages use an imperative subject under 72 chars, and the body says why.
128|
129|## Design
130|
131|Minimalist, functional, elegant. No generic AI-template look: no purple or violet anywhere, no gradient blobs, no glassmorphism, no emoji icons, no stock hero sections.
132|
133|The palette comes from Meta's brand. Meta blue `#0866FF` is the single accent, `#0064E0` for hover and pressed states. Text is near-black `#1C2B33`. Surfaces are white `#FFFFFF` and soft gray `#F1F4F7`. Dark mode keeps the same accent on a near-black surface: `#0B1215` surface, `#E4E6EB` text.
134|
135|The layout is typography-first. The book sits centered with a comfortable measure, about 60 to 70 chars per line. The companion chat lives in a quiet side panel. Whitespace is generous, the accent color is single, motion is subtle: under 200 ms, and it respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.
136|
137|These values live as CSS custom properties in [app/tokens.css](app/tokens.css), which is the source of truth.
138|
139|## Hooks
140|
141|`npm install` (or `npm run prepare`) points `core.hooksPath` at `.githooks`. The `pre-commit` hook rejects staged files over 5000 tokens and staged secrets. The `prepare-commit-msg` hook adds the co-author trailer. Run the checks by hand with `npm run check:size` and `npm run check:secrets`, and the hook tests with `npm run test:hooks`.

65|## Workflow
66|
67|Each task follows the same loop. Muse Spark 1.3 Standard (`muse-spark-1.3`) writes the design in `docs/tasks/NN-name.md`; the orchestrating agent writes the review in `docs/reviews/NN.md`. `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` implements. Implement and review run at most two rounds.
68|
69|A rescue by another tool happens only after those rounds. Log it in `RESCUE_LOG.md` with the date, the task, the tool, why Muse got stuck, what changed, and the commits. Rescue commits carry a `Rescue: <tool>` trailer and no Muse Code trailer; the hook skips them.
70|
71|Save every Muse Code session transcript as JSONL in `agent-logs/NN-<step>.jsonl`. Commits Muse Code wrote carry the Muse Code co-author trailer, which the `prepare-commit-msg` hook adds. 73|## Lectoria rules
74|
75|- The text unit is the scene, not the paragraph or chapter.
76|- Paragraph ids are global, like `c12p34`.
77|- The emotion taxonomy has 8 ASCII ids: calma, alegria, tristeza, suspenso, misterio, aventura, combate, asombro. 78|- Jev runs at `POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone` with the model pinned to `jev-1.14.0`.
79|- Public-domain books only.
80|- Images follow the book text and the W. W. Denslow 1900 illustrations: silver shoes, nothing from the 1939 MGM film.
81|- Never copy code from github.com/martinmw13/lectoria.
82|- Test with the cheapest models (Contributor). Use Standard for the final pass and the public chat.
83|
84|## Product rules
85|
86|Owner decisions. Short and binding.
87|
88|- Desktop first. No mobile or iOS work now.
89|- The reader shows one scene at a time. Sub-pages split long scenes by length only. Music cues run on scene entry.
90|- A chapter holds several scenes. Each scene has its own emotion.
91|- Paragraph ids carry a global ordinal `n`. Compare `n`, never id strings.
92|- `book.json` is frozen with a `textVersion` hash. Every cache key includes it.
93|- Scenes cover each chapter's paragraphs with no gaps and no overlaps. No scene crosses a chapter boundary. Scenes split at strong sequential emotion shifts; blends stay in the vector.
94|- Emotions are distributions. Each scene stores the full Jev probability vector over the 8 ids, plus `intensity` (0 to 1) and `tempo` (energy, 0 to 1). The Muse override on low confidence edits the vector and records that it did. It never swaps in a single label.
95|- Music is about 15 tracks, pre-generated offline with MusicGen on Modal as one coherent soundtrack: same orchestra and instrumentation, same leitmotif style. 96|- The player picks the track nearest to the scene vector, by cosine similarity over the vector plus intensity and tempo. Hysteresis stops it from flipping on small changes. Skip or change track overrides until the next scene.
97|- The owner listens to short clips before any full generation. Agents do not run Modal until the owner says so.
98|- MusicGen weights are CC-BY-NC. The hackathon demo is non-commercial. The generated tracks must say so in their README.
99|- Chat is low priority and simple. The context is the book text up to the reader's current position. The book prefix goes first and the question goes last, so readers share the prompt cache. Oz is about 55k tokens.
100|- The chat system prompt answers only from the provided text. It refuses knowledge beyond it, even if the model knows the book.
101|- A spoiler mode toggle is for readers who finished the book. It sends the whole text so they can ask about later events. No live Glimmer spoiler guard. No per-chapter summaries for chat. Citing passages is optional.
102|- Glimmer (open weights) keeps a pipeline role. Current decision: it writes the per-scene "why this music" explanation shown in the Developer View.
103|- Spikes come before feature code. Throwaway scripts in `scripts/spikes/` measure Muse Image (response format, latency, Denslow-style prompt), Meta `json_schema` structured output, and the Jev vector on a few Oz scenes. Results go to `docs/spikes.md`.
104|- Spend is counted in integer micro-dollars. Reserve with Redis `INCRBY` before each model call and refund with `DECRBY` after. Reserve per call, including retries.
105|- The server clamps every model tool argument. Tool arguments are untrusted input.
106|- The CSP allows `challenges.cloudflare.com` (script and frame) and `*.public.blob.vercel-storage.com` (images).
107|- The "Picture this" cache key is the book plus the selection's paragraph range plus `textVersion` plus `promptVersion`. A selection that overlaps a cached range in the same scene with paragraph Jaccard at least 1/3 reuses that image; a much larger, smaller, or disjoint one gets its own. The prompt is built from the selected paragraphs plus scene context.
108|- Chapter panels (one comic page per chapter) are drawn only for chapters the reader has reached: requests carry `reachedCh` and the server refuses `ch > reachedCh`. It is the client's claim, since there is no server-side reading position.
109|- The "Picture scene" cache key is the book plus the scene id plus `textVersion` plus `promptVersion`.
110|- Images live in Vercel Blob at deterministic public paths (`addRandomSuffix: false`, `allowOverwrite: false`). An index in Upstash Redis maps key to Blob URL so hits are one Redis GET; on an index miss check the Blob path with `head()` before generating and backfill the index. Routes return Blob URLs, never image bytes.
111|- Modal endpoints require proxy auth. Tokens live only in env.
112|
113|## Security rules
114|
115|Summary. The full rules live in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).
116|
117|- Secrets live only in env vars: `.env.local` locally (gitignored), Vercel env vars in prod.
118|- `.env.example` holds names only, never values.
119|- Never use a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variable for a secret. Only public ids such as the Turnstile site key may use it.
120|- `core/` stays pure: no keys, no env reads, no network clients, no `server-only`. 122|- Errors to the client are generic. Details go to server logs only, never with keys.
123|- Never log request headers.

126|
127|Run docs, UI copy, and commit messages through the `unslop` skill: no filler, no hype, no emoji in headings, none of seamless, elevate, delve, robust, leverage. Headings use sentence case. Commit messages use an imperative subject under 72 chars, and the body says why.

130|
131|Minimalist, functional, elegant. No generic AI-template look: no purple or violet anywhere, no gradient blobs, no glassmorphism, no emoji icons, no stock hero sections.
132|
133|The palette comes from Meta's brand. Meta blue `#0866FF` is the single accent, `#0064E0` for hover and pressed states. Text is near-black `#1C2B33`. Surfaces are white `#FFFFFF` and soft gray `#F1F4F7`. Dark mode keeps the same accent on a near-black surface: `#0B1215` surface, `#E4E6EB` text.
